2. CHINA/RUSSIA/KAZAKHSTAN: CATCHING FALLING STARS
(12/25)

CHINESE LEADERS ARE WATCHING SOVIET DISSOLUTION WITH

                                      DECLASSIFIED/RELEASE IN FULL
                                 MARVIN RUSSELL, SENIOR REVIEWER

DEEP UNEASE BUT ARE BEGINNING TO FORGE TIES WITH RUSSIA
AND KAZAKHSTAN. NOT SURPRISINGLY, CONSERVATIVES AND
REFORMERS HAVE DRAWN DIFFERENT LESSONS FOR CHINA FROM
THE SOVIET COLLAPSE.

3. DISMAYED BY THE SOVIET COLLAPSE, CHINESE LEADERS
HAVE PUBLICLY VOICED CONCERN OVER CONTROL OF THE SOVIET
NUCLEAR ARSENAL AND A POSSIBLE FLOOD OF REFUGEES. IN
PRIVATE THEY EXPRESS FEARS OF REVIVED RUSSIAN
NATIONALISM AND OF ETHNIC UNREST SPREADING TO CHINA:
BEIJING HAS INCREASED MILITARY READINESS AND STEPPED UP
SECURITY MEASURES TO CONTROL ETHNIC MINORITIES IN BORDER
AREAS.

4. THE SOVIET BREAKUP HAS AMBIGUOUS MILITARY,
POLITICAL. AND ECONOMIC CONSEQUENCES FOR CHINA. LEADERS
SEE A LONG PERIOD OF TURMOIL AKIN TO CHINA'S CULTURAL
REVOLUTION WITH CONTINUED ECONOMIC DECLINE, GROWING
CIVIL UNREST AND THE LIKELIHOOD OF FURTHER COUP
ATTEMPTS. NOT WANTING TO HASTEN THE SOVIET BREAKUP,
CHINESE LEADERS HELD BACK FROM BUILDING TIES TO NEW
REPUBLICAN LEADERS; THEY GRATUITOUSLY SNUBBED YELTSIN
AND UNTIL TWO WEEKS AGO, DEALT WITH THE USSR GOVERNMENT
ON BORDER ISSUES.

5. DEALING WITH THE REPUBLICS. CHINA'S INTEREST IN THE
REPUBLICS ORIGINALLY STIMULATED BY TAIWAN'S ACTIVIST
DIPLOMACY TOWARD THESE EMERGING TARGETS OF OPPORTUNITY,
HAS NOW TAKEN ON GREAT URGENCY. BEIJING ANNOUNCED
DECEMBER 24 IT WAS READY TO ESTABLISH RELATIONS WITH THE
NEW COMMONWEALTH REPUBLICS, AND IT WILL PROBABLY DO SO
                8-E-eR-ET



PAGE 03    STATE  011627 140856Z
JUST AFTER GORBACHEV RESIGNS; IT RECENTLY WELCOMED A
REPRESENTATIVE OF YELTSIN AND HAS REPORTEDLY INVITED
RUSSIA'S FOREIGN MINISTER TO VISIT BEIJING.

6. THIS WEEK IT SIGNED A NEW TRADE PACT WITH
KAZAKHSTAN THOUGH IT HAS NOT ACTED ON A KAZAKH PROPOSAL
TO SET UP CONSULATES IN URUMQI AND ALMA ATA. FEARING
TURKIC NATIONALIST CONTAGION FROM CENTRAL ASIA, BEIJING
IS UNLIKELY SOON TO WELCOME CONSULAR MISSIONS IN
XINJIANG.

7. CHINA'S LEADERS REMAIN UNCOMFORTABLE DEALING WITH
THE REPUBLICS AND THEIR APOSTATE COMMUNIST LEADERS AND




                  UNCLASSIFIED

                                                               Page 2 of 4

M-2018-02711   B-00002673717    UNCLASSIFIED    10/9/2026

                   [UNCLASSIFIED





CONTINUE TO HEDGE THEIR BETS. XINHUA, FOR INSTANCE, HAS
CONSISTENTLY REPORTED EVIDENCE, NOT HIGHLIGHTED BY
WESTERN MEDIA OF A POSSIBLE REVIVAL OF COMMUNIST
FORTUNES. THOUGH ANTEDATING THE MINSK AGREEMENT,
CHINESE TRADE ORGANIZATIONS WERE RECENTLY DIRECTED TO
CONDUCT MORE BUSINESS WITH SOVIET STATE ENTERPRISES IN
ORDER TO SUPPORT THE CENTRAL GOVERNMENT AND,
INCONGRUOUSLY THE CPSU, ACCORDING TO AN UNTESTED

SOURCE. AT BORDER CONFIDENCE-BUILDING TALKS IN MOSCOW
LAST MONTH, CHINA REPORTEDLY BACKED AWAY FROM PREVIOUS
POSITIONS FEARING THE REFUBLICS MIGHT BACKTRACK ON
TENTATIVE AGREEMENTS AND TAKE CHINA'S FINAL POSITION AS
A NEGOTIATING STARTING POINT.

8. LESSONS FOR CHINA. CHINESE LEADERS INTERPRET SOVIET
COLLAPSE AS EVIDENCE THEIR OWN ECONOMIC REFORM POLICIES
AND "RESOLUTE MEASURES" TO RESLVE THE TIANANMEN




PAGE 04    STATE  011627 140856Z
"TURMOIL" SAVED CHINA FROM CHAOS AND WESTERN
SUBVERSION. THEY DISSOCIATE CHINA FROM THE USSR AND
STRESS THE UNIQUENESS OF CHINESE COMMUNISM AND ITS
NATIONALIST ROOTS, TO COUNTER ANY POPULAR NOTION THAT
COMMUNISM'S DAYS IN CHINA ARE NUMBERED. BUT EMBASSY
BEIJING REPORTS AN ALMOST NON-STOP ROUND OF MEETINGS IN
RECENT WEEKS ON SOVIET DEVELOPMENTS TO FIX THE "LESSONS"
FOR CHINA. CONSERVATIVES AND MODERATES DRAW OPPOSING
CONCLUSIONS. CONSERVATIVES MAINTAIN THAT POLITICAL
REFORM CAUSED THE CPSU'S DOWNFALL AND ARGUE FOR GREATER
IDEOLOGICAL DISCIPLINE; MODERATES, INCLUDING PARTY CHIEF
JIANG ZEMIN, ASSERT THE CPSU COLLAPSED BECAUSE ITS
LEADERS LOST TOUCH WITH THE MASSES AND ARGUE FOR
CONTINUING. EVEN INTENSIFYING, REFORM IN CHINA.
(JHUSKEY)

document_candidates.title: U.S.-RUSSIAN-UKRAINIAN TRILATERAL DISCUSSION
document_candidates.repository: U.S. Department of State FOIA Library
document_candidates.action: Directly relevant to Volume XX: the report examines the U.S.–Russian–Ukrainian process for deactivating strategic nuclear weapons in Ukraine, warhead removal and HEU blending, START silo dismantlement, and NPT conditions.
document_candidates.reportingDateNote: Cable date: August 30, 1993. The report summarizes trilateral talks in London on August 26 and a Moscow meeting on August 28.
document_candidates.copyCitation: U.S. Department of State, Embassy Moscow, telegram 1993 MOSCOW 027244, “U.S.-RUSSIAN-UKRAINIAN TRILATERAL DISCUSSION,” 1993-08-30, FOIA Library, case M-2017-11832, document C09000003, source PDF, pp. 1–7.
document_candidates.summary: A report of talks with Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mamedov on how to proceed with a U.S.–Russian–Ukrainian arrangement for deactivating nuclear weapons in Ukraine, including warhead removal, blending highly enriched uranium, START dismantlement procedures, and NPT adherence.
document_candidates.relevance: The source directly addresses arms control and nuclear nonproliferation involving Ukraine and Russia within the volume's December 1991–December 1994 scope. It is a documentary lead, not a selection decision.

3. ACTION REQUEST: SEE PARA 13.

4. SUMMARY: ON AUGUST 28 AMBASSADOR PICKERING MET
RUSSIAN DEPUTY FOREIGN MINISTER MAMEDOV TO REVIEW THE
AUGUST 26 TRILATERAL TALKS IN LONDON:

-- MAMEDOV WELCOMED THE U.S. APPROACH TO THE EARLY

DEACTIVIZATION ISSUE AND THE EXPLANATION AMBASSADOR

TALBOTT HAD GIVEN OF THE CLINTON ADMINISTRATION'S NEW
SECRET

APPROACH TO DEALING WITH UKRAINE, WHICH COULD ALSO
HELP IN DEALING WITH SKEPTICS IN MOSCOW.

-- MAMEDOV WELCOMED THE U.S. DECISION TO DO NOTHING

IN ITS CONTACTS WITH UKRAINE THAT WOULD UNDERMINE THE
RUSSIAN-UKRAINIAN BILATERAL APPROACH. MAMEDOV SAID

HE WOULD BE WORKING INTENSIVELY ON GETTING AN
AGREEMENT WITH THE UKRAINIANS BY THE SEPTEMBER 3
YELTSIN-KRAVCHUK SUMMIT, ALTHOUGH HE CONCEDED THAT IT
MIGHT NOT BE POSSIBLE BY THAT MEETING TO NAIL DOWN A
TIME FRAME FOR DEACTIVIZATION.

-- MAMEDOV NOTED U.S. SKEPTICISM THAT THE BILATERAL
APPROACH COULD SUCCEED; THAT SKEPTICISM WAS SHARED IN
MOSCOW, IN PART BECAUSE THE BILATERAL ACCORD HAD
BECOME INVOLVED IN UKRAINIAN INFIGHTING.
